item.title: How Does the Iran War Affect China’s Energy Security?
item.description: Since the beginning of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, a key question constantly asked is how Beijing might react — assuming that China’s economy relies on oil imported from Iran and shipped through the Strait of Hormuz.In reality, however, China is 85 percent energy self-sufficient. While China imports more than 10 percent of its global oil total from Iran, its energy supply has long been diversified internationally and electrified domestically to avoid critical dependence on any single source. item.title: Takeaways from China’s National People’s Congress Meeting
item.description: From March 5 to 12, China held its annual Two Sessions — the National People’s Congress meeting and the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. These gatherings provide yearly insights into China’s economic and political priorities and plans. Additionally, this year, the government presented its 15th Five-Year Plan, laying out key policies to 2030. item.description: In recent years, as AI has begun to enter military planning and operational design, a persistent unease has surfaced among practitioners. item.title: The Inevitability of Chinese Military Purges
item.description: The scale of Secretary General Xi Jinping’s military purges is shocking. More than 100 senior leaders have been removed since 2022. item.title: Countering Drones and the Pace of Modern War
item.description: This episode is about far more than countering drones. It is about how America prepares for and fights its wars.
